claims.claim: Reducing ilp6 in cardiac cells augments PSC cell number without affecting crystal cell differentiation.
claims.source: Reducing ilp6 in cardiac cells (d, d') augments PSC cell number (e) without affecting crystal cell differentiation (f); this defines class 1.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1c-f.

claims.claim: Knocking down dachsous (ds) in cardiac cells decreases PSC cell number and increases crystal cell index.
claims.source: Knocking down dachsous (ds) in cardiac cells (g, g') decreases PSC cell number (h) and increases crystal cell index (i); this defines class 2.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1g-i.

claims.claim: Reducing pvf3 in cardiac cells does not modify PSC cell number but increases crystal cell differentiation.
claims.source: Reducing pvf3 in cardiac cells (j, j') does not modify PSC cell number (k) but increases crystal cell differentiation (l); this defines class 3.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1j-l.

claims.claim: Decrease in tep4 expression is observed when pvf3 is knocked down in cardiac cells.
claims.source: tep4 (red) labels core progenitors. Decrease in tep4 expression is observed when pvf3 is knocked down in cardiac cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1m-o.

claims.claim: 17 RNAi lines showed lymph gland homeostasis defects out of 49 Drosophila ligands screened.
claims.source: Compared to the control, 17 RNAi lines showed lymph gland homeostasis defects that were classified into three groups (Figure 1b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the screen results shown in Figure 1b.

claims.claim: Reduced tep4 expression was observed for 12 RNAi treatments out of 14 in class 3.
claims.source: Reduced tep4 expression was observed for 12 RNAi treatments out of 14 (Figure 1m–o andsource data), indicating that the corresponding genes are required in cardiac cells to maintain tep4 expression in lymph gland progenitors and to prevent crystal cell differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data from the screen and tep4 in situ hybridization.

claims.claim: Nine ligands were identified as involved in communication between cardiac cells and hematopoietic progenitors to control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.source: In conclusion, our functional screen allowed us to identify nine ligands involved in communication between cardiac cells and hematopoietic progenitors to control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the screen results using two independent cardiac drivers.

claims.claim: Htl-FGF signaling is required during both early embryogenesis for lymph gland specification and in L3 larvae to control lymph gland progenitors.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that Htl-FGF signaling is required during both early embryogenesis for lymph gland specification (Grigorian et al., 2013; Mandal et al., 2007) and in L3 larvae to control lymph gland progenitors (Dragojlovic-Munther and Martinez-Agosto, 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: No role for bnl in the lymph gland has been described yet.
claims.source: However, no role for bnl in the lymph gland has been described yet.
claims.evidence: This statement is based on the absence of prior literature on bnl function in the lymph gland.

claims.claim: bnl is expressed in cardiac and pericardial cells.
claims.source: bnl is expressed in cardiac and pericardial cells (Figure 2a–a''), in agreement with previously published data (Jarecki et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a-a'' and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: A weak bnl expression is observed in MZ progenitors.
claims.source: We also observed a weak bnl expression in MZ progenitors (as labeled by domeMESO >GFP in Figure 2a–a"), in differentiating hemocytes (as labeled by hml >GFP) and in a subset of crystal cells (marked by BcGFP) whereas no expression was detected in the PSC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–c").
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a-a'' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: In a heterozygous bnl loss-of-function mutant context (bnlP2/+), an increased number of crystal cells was observed compared to the control.
claims.source: In a heterozygous bnl loss-of-function mutant context where one copy of bnl (bnlP2/+) is missing, we observed an increased number of crystal cells compared to the control (Figure 2b–d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2b-d.

claims.claim: bnl down-regulation in cardiac cells resulted in increased differentiation of both crystal cells and plasmatocytes.
claims.source: bnl down-regulation in cardiac cells resulted in increased differentiation of both crystal cells and plasmatocytes (Figure 2e–f,i and Figure 2—figure supplement 1f–h).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: A reduced expression of DomeMESO-RFP, tep4, and Col was observed when bnl was knocked down in cardiac cells.
claims.source: Compared to wild type, a reduced expression of the three markers was observed in handΔ>bnl-RNAi lymph glands (Figure 2j–r), indicating that Bnl from cardiac cells non-cell autonomously controls MZ progenitor maintenance.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2j-r.

claims.claim: Bnl produced in the cardiac tube acts in third instar larvae to control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.source: Altogether, these data indicate that Bnl produced in the cardiac tube acts in third instar larvae to control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental results showing bnl knockdown effects.

claims.claim: Reduction of bnl expression in progenitors led to a significant increase in crystal cell differentiation as well as a decrease in tep4 expression.
claims.source: Reduction of bnl expression in progenitors (dome >bnl-RNAi) led to a significant increase in crystal cell differentiation as well as a decrease in tep4 expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f), indicating that Bnl produced by MZ progenitors is required to maintain their identity and to prevent their differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a-f.

claims.claim: Bnl is produced by both MZ and cardiac cells, and both sources are required in the control of lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.source: Altogether, these data show that Bnl is produced by both MZ and cardiac cells, and that both sources are required in the control of lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data showing bnl expression and functional requirements in both cell types.

claims.claim: When bnl was knocked down only in the cardiac tube, a reduction of bnl:GFPendo was observed both in cardiac cells and MZ progenitors.
claims.source: However, when bnl was knocked down only in the cardiac tube (handΔ>bnl-RNAi, bnl:GFPendo; Figure 2t–u) we overserved a reduction of bnl:GFPendo both in cardiac cells and MZ progenitors thus establishing that Bnl produced by cardiac cells contributes to the global MZ Bnl pool.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2t-u using the bnl:GFPendo knock-in allele.

claims.claim: Overexpression of bnl only in cardiac cells led to reduced crystal cell numbers.
claims.source: To further support this conclusion, we overexpressed bnl only in cardiac cells (handΔ>bnl) which led to reduced crystal cell numbers (Figure 2i), and this confirms that the level of Bnl produced by cardiac cells controls hemocyte differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2i.

claims.claim: Rescue of crystal cell numbers and progenitor marker expression was observed with simultaneous expression of bnl and bnl-RNAi in cardiac cells.
claims.source: Finally, rescue of crystal cell numbers (Figure 2g–i) and of progenitor marker expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g–i) was observed with a simultaneous expression of bnl and bnl-RNAi in cardiac cells (handΔ>bnl; bnl-RNAi).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 2g-i and Figure 2—figure supplement 2g-i.

claims.claim: Cardiac cell Bnl neither affects PSC cell numbers nor Hh activity.
claims.source: These data strongly suggest that cardiac cell Bnl neither affects PSC cell numbers nor Hh activity, and likely acts directly on MZ progenitors to control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data showing no changes in PSC markers when bnl is knocked down in cardiac cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2j-o).

claims.claim: Strong btl:cherryendo expression was observed in cardiac cells and lower levels in MZ progenitors.
claims.source: Strong btl:cherryendo expression was observed in cardiac cells and lower levels in MZ progenitors (as labeled by domeMESO-GFP in Figure 3a–a").
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data using the btl:cherryendo knock-in allele shown in Figure 3a-a''.

claims.claim: No btl:cherryendo expression was detected in PSC cells.
claims.source: Whereas no expression was detected in PSC cells, a very faint expression occurs in a subset of crystal cells and in most differentiating blood cells (labeled by BcGFP and Hml >GFP, respectively, in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a–c").
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a-c''.

claims.claim: Crystal cell differentiation is increased in btldev1/+ heterozygous mutant larvae compared to the control.
claims.source: The resulting crystal cell index was higher than in controls (Figure 3b–d), revealing that btl controls lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3b-d.

claims.claim: btl downregulation in cardiac cells did not significantly affect crystal cell numbers or MZ progenitors.
claims.source: btl downregulation in cardiac cells did not significantly affect crystal cell numbers or MZ progenitors (Figure 3—figure supplement 1d–i).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1d-i.

claims.claim: Knocking down btl in MZ progenitors led to increased crystal cell and plasmatocyte numbers, together with reduced expression of domeMESO-LacZ and tep4.
claims.source: In contrast, knocking down btl in MZ progenitors led to increased crystal cell (Figure 3e,g) and plasmatocyte numbers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1j–l), together with a reduced expression of the two progenitor markers domeMESO-LacZ and tep4 (Figure 3h–m).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The expression of btlCA in progenitors led to reduced crystal cell numbers.
claims.source: The expression of btlCA in progenitors (dome >btlCA) led to reduced crystal cell numbers, i.e., a phenotype opposite to that of btl loss-of-function (Figure 3g).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3g.

claims.claim: The co-expression of btlCA and btl-RNAi in progenitors rescued crystal cell differentiation.
claims.source: The co-expression of btlCA and btl-RNAi in progenitors (dome >btl-RNAi>btlCA; Figure 3f,g) rescued crystal cell differentiation, confirming that Btl is required in MZ progenitors.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 3f-g.

claims.claim: No difference in PSC cell numbers or clustering was observed when btl was knocked down in progenitors.
claims.source: Finally, we examined whether PSC cells were affected when btl was knocked down in progenitors. No difference in PSC cell numbers or clustering was observed compared to the control (Figure 3—figure supplement 1m–o).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1m-o.

claims.claim: btl expression in MZ progenitors is required to control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.source: We conclude that btl expression in MZ progenitors is required to control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is supported by multiple experimental results showing btl knockdown and rescue effects.

claims.claim: Expression of a dominant–negative form of Htl in progenitors led to a decrease in crystal cell differentiation.
claims.source: Expression of a dominant–negative form of Htl (dome >HtlDN) in progenitors led to a decrease in crystal cell differentiation, in agreement with a previous report (Dragojlovic-Munther and Martinez-Agosto, 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3n-p and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Simultaneous expression of HtlDN and btl-RNAi restored a wildtype number of crystal cells.
claims.source: Simultaneous expression of HtlDN and btl-RNAi (dome >HtlDN > btl-RNAi) restored a wildtype number of crystal cells (Figure 3n–p).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by epistasis experiment data shown in Figure 3n-p.

claims.claim: There is no hierarchy between Btl-FGF and Htl-FGF pathways.
claims.source: These data indicate that there is no hierarchy between Btl-FGF and Htl-FGF pathways.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the epistasis experiment results.

claims.claim: The simultaneous activity of Btl-FGF and Htl-FGF pathways in MZ progenitors ensures a robust regulation of hemocyte differentiation.
claims.source: They also suggest that their simultaneous activity in MZ progenitors ensures a robust regulation of hemocyte differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the epistasis results.

claims.claim: Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling mediates inter-organ communication between MZ progenitors and the vascular system.
claims.source: This strongly suggests that Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling mediates inter-organ communication between MZ progenitors and the vascular system.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is supported by the combined results showing bnl in cardiac cells and btl in progenitors.

claims.claim: The cardiac tube plays a role similar to a niche by acting directly on MZ progenitors.
claims.source: This leads us to propose that by acting directly on MZ progenitors, the cardiac tube plays a role similar to a niche.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the functional data.

claims.claim: Discrete GFP positive cytoplasmic punctate dots/granules were detected in MZ progenitors when Bnl::GFP was expressed in cardiac cells.
claims.source: In addition to the expected GFP detection in these cells, discrete GFP positive cytoplasmic punctate dots/granules were detected in MZ progenitors (Figure 4a–a''), indicating that Bnl::GFP can propagate from cardiac to lymph gland cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4a-a''.

claims.claim: Many cytoplasmic Bnl-GFP positive punctate dots in the MZ were Btl:Cherry positive.
claims.source: Many cytoplasmic Bnl-GFP positive punctate dots in the MZ were Btl:Cherry positive (Figure 4b–b").
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 4b-b''.

claims.claim: Many Rab11-positive and Rab7-positive vesicles co-localized with Bnl-GFP in the MZ.
claims.source: We found that many Rab11-positive and Rab7-positive vesicles co-localized with Bnl-GFP in the MZ (Figure 4c–d").
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 4c-d''.

claims.claim: Bnl::GFP secreted by cardiac cells is internalized by MZ progenitors, likely through receptor-mediated endocytosis.
claims.source: The simplest explanation is that Bnl::GFP secreted by cardiac cells is internalized by MZ progenitors, likely through receptor-mediated endocytosis.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on the co-localization with endosomal markers.

claims.claim: The simultaneous expression of sar1-RNAi and Bnl::GFP in cardiac cells resulted in reduced bnl::GFP cytoplasmic punctate dots in MZ progenitors compared to the control.
claims.source: The simultaneous expression of sar1-RNAi and Bnl::GFP in cardiac cells using the handΔ-gal4 driver (handΔ>bnl::GFP >sar1 RNAi) resulted in reduced bnl::GFP cytoplasmic punctate dots in MZ progenitors compared to the control (Figure 4e–g), further confirming that cardiac cells secrete Bnl.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4e-g.

claims.claim: When sar1 was knocked down in cardiac cells, an increase in PSC cell numbers as well as a slight defect in their clustering was observed.
claims.source: Consistent with the impairment of cardiac cell secretion when sar1 is knocked down in cardiac cells (handΔ>and NP1029>sar1 RNAi, Figure 4—figure supplement 1a–f), we also observed an increase in PSC cell numbers as well as a slight defect in their clustering, likely an effect of Slit/Robo impairment.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a-f.

claims.claim: When sar1 was knocked down in cardiac cells, crystal cell numbers were higher than the control.
claims.source: When sar1 was knocked down in cardiac cells using handΔ or NP1029 drivers (Figure 4h–i,k and Figure 4—figure supplement 1g–i) crystal cell numbers were higher than the control, indicating that cardiac cell secretion capacity is necessary for lymph gland hematopoiesis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4h-k and Figure 4—figure supplement 1g-i.

claims.claim: Crystal cell differentiation was improved when sar1-RNAi and bnl::GFP were simultaneously expressed in cardiac cells.
claims.source: Crystal cell differentiation was improved when sar1-RNAi and bnl::GFP were simultaneously expressed in cardiac cells (Figure 4j,k).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 4j-k.

claims.claim: Bnl secreted by cardiac cells is likely taken up by MZ progenitors to activate Btl-FGF signaling, which in turn regulates lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.source: In conclusion, these results indicate that Bnl secreted by cardiac cells is likely taken up by MZ progenitors to activate Btl-FGF signaling, which in turn regulates lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined results of Bnl secretion and uptake experiments.

claims.claim: Inactivation of MAPK or PI3K in lymph gland progenitors leads to a phenotype opposite to that of knock-down of btl in progenitors or of bnl in cardiac cells.
claims.source: Inactivation of MAPK or PI3K in lymph gland progenitors leads to a phenotype opposite to that of knock-down of btl in progenitors or of bnl in cardiac cells (Dragojlovic-Munther and Martinez-Agosto, 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling in progenitors does not involve MAPK or PI3K activity.
claims.source: This strongly suggests that Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling in progenitors does not involve MAPK or PI3K activity.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the opposite phenotypes observed.

claims.claim: Reduction of cytosolic Ca2+ in lymph gland progenitors leads to the loss of progenitor markers and to increased blood cell differentiation.
claims.source: It was previously reported that intracellular Ca2+ levels regulate hematopoietic progenitor maintenance: reduction of cytosolic Ca2+ in lymph gland progenitors leads to the loss of progenitor markers and to increased blood cell differentiation (Shim et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: High Ca2+ levels were detected in MZ progenitors.
claims.source: In agreement with previous reports, high Ca2+ levels were detected in MZ progenitors (Figure 5a and Shim et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data using the GCaMP3 sensor shown in Figure 5a and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Knocking down btl in MZ progenitors starting from L1 stage led in third instar larvae to decreased fluorescence of the Ca2+ sensor, indicating a reduction in Ca2+ levels.
claims.source: Knocking down btl in MZ progenitors starting from L1 stage led in third instar larvae to decreased fluorescence compared to the control, indicating a reduction in Ca2+ levels (Figure 5a–c).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5a-c.

claims.claim: No difference in Ca2+ levels was observed at L2 stage when btl was knocked down.
claims.source: Since no difference with control larvae could be observed at L2 stage (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a–c), we conclude that the Bnl/Btl-FGF pathway is not required for MZ progenitor specification but is required in third instar larvae to regulate Ca2+ levels.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1a-c.

claims.claim: The Bnl/Btl-FGF pathway is not required for MZ progenitor specification but is required in third instar larvae to regulate Ca2+ levels.
claims.source: Since no difference with control larvae could be observed at L2 stage (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a–c), we conclude that the Bnl/Btl-FGF pathway is not required for MZ progenitor specification but is required in third instar larvae to regulate Ca2+ levels.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the temporal analysis of Ca2+ levels.

claims.claim: Overexpression of CaMKII or IP3R in progenitors led to a significant decrease in crystal cell numbers compared to the control.
claims.source: When free Ca2+ was high within the progenitors, such as following overexpression of Calmodulin dependent kinase II (CaMKII; dome >CaMKII) or of IP3R (Tep4 >UAS-IP3R) which controls ER-mediated Ca2+ release into the cytosol (Shim et al., 2013), a significant decrease in crystal cell numbers was observed compared to the control (Figure 5d–h and Figure 5—figure supplement 1d–h).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5d-h and Figure 5—figure supplement 1d-h.

claims.claim: High Ca2+ levels in progenitors inhibit blood cell differentiation.
claims.source: This indicates that high Ca2+ levels in progenitors inhibit blood cell differentiation, which is in agreement with previously published data (Shim et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Simultaneous btl reduction and Ca2+ increase in progenitors leads to a decrease in crystal cell numbers compared to the sole btl-RNAi knockdown.
claims.source: Simultaneous btl reduction and Ca2+ increase in progenitors, through CaMKII or IP3R overexpression (dome >CamKII;btl-RNAi Figure 5g–h and tep4 >IP3R>btl-RNAi; Figure 5—figure supplement 1g–h), leads to a decrease in crystal cell numbers compared to the sole btl-RNAi knockdown.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 5g-h and Figure 5—figure supplement 1g-h.

claims.claim: In MZ progenitors, regulation of Ca2+ levels functions downstream of the Bnl/Btl-FGF pathway.
claims.source: Overall, these data suggest that in MZ progenitors, regulation of Ca2+ levels functions downstream of the Bnl/Btl-FGF pathway.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the rescue experiments.

claims.claim: Increased crystal cell differentiation was observed in strong hypomorphic sl2 mutants compared to the control.
claims.source: To investigate the role of PLCγ in the lymph gland, we analyzed crystal cell differentiation in strong hypomorphic sl2 mutants. Compared to the control, increased crystal cell differentiation was observed (as labeled by Hnt Figure 5j,m).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5j,m.

claims.claim: Knocking down PLCγ in progenitors led to increased crystal cell differentiation compared to the control.
claims.source: Knocking down PLCγ in progenitors (dome >sl-RNAi) led to increased crystal cell differentiation compared to the control (Figure 5i,l), revealing that PLCγ in MZ progenitors regulates lymph gland hemocyte differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5i,l.

claims.claim: When btlCA was expressed in progenitors in a sl2 mutant context, the crystal cell index was similar to that in the sl2 mutant alone.
claims.source: When btlCA was expressed in progenitors in a sl2 mutant context (sl2; dome >bltCA; Figure 5k,n), the crystal cell index was similar to that in the sl2 mutant alone.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by epistasis experiment data shown in Figure 5k,n.

claims.claim: sl acts downstream of the Bnl/Btl-FGF pathway.
claims.source: These data establish that sl acts downstream of the Bnl/Btl-FGF pathway.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the epistasis experiment results.

claims.claim: In MZ progenitors, Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling leads to the activation of PLCγ, which controls Ca2+ levels and in turn hemocyte differentiation.
claims.source: Altogether, our data support the hypothesis that in MZ progenitors, Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling leads to the activation of PLCγ, which controls Ca2+ levels and in turn hemocyte differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the combined results of Ca2+ and PLCγ experiments.

claims.claim: A subset of lymph gland progenitors (core progenitors), which express Col and tep4 and are aligned along the cardiac tube, is maintained in the lymph gland even when the PSC function is impaired.
claims.source: However, a subset of lymph gland progenitors (core progenitors), which express Col and tep4 and are aligned along the cardiac tube, is maintained in the lymph gland even when the PSC function is impaired, suggesting that other signals alongside those from the PSC are required (Baldeosingh et al., 2018; Benmimoun et al., 2015; Oyallon et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Cardiac cells play a role similar to a niche, since they directly control core progenitor maintenance.
claims.source: Here, we report that cardiac cells play a role similar to a niche, since they directly control core progenitor maintenance.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study.

claims.claim: Communication between the vascular system and the lymph gland involves Bnl/Btl-FGFsignaling.
claims.source: We show that communication between the vascular system and the lymph gland involves Bnl/Btl-FGFsignaling.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claims.claim: Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling regulates lymph gland homeostasis by controlling calcium levels in progenitors via PLCγ activation.
claims.source: Our data indicate that Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling regulates lymph gland homeostasis by controlling calcium levels in progenitors via PLCγ activation (Figure 6).
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study illustrated in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Signals from the cardiac tube, namely Slit, can act on the PSC, but no cellular communication between the cardiac tube and MZ progenitors is involved in this pathway.
claims.source: In a previous study, we showed that signals from the cardiac tube, namely Slit, can act on the PSC, but that no cellular communication between the cardiac tube and MZ progenitors is involved (Morin-Poulard et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claims.claim: Cardiac cells regulate the extent of progenitor differentiation in the lymph gland.
claims.source: Now we establish that cardiac cells regulate the extent of progenitor differentiation in the lymph gland.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the current study.

claims.claim: Two separate niches (the PSC and the cardiac tube) control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.source: Therefore, two separate niches (the PSC and the cardiac tube) control lymph gland homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study.

claims.claim: The PSC acts only on a subset of MZ progenitors.
claims.source: While the PSC acts only on a subset of MZ progenitors (Baldeosingh et al., 2018; Oyallon et al., 2016), the cardiac tube directly regulates core progenitors and in turn all MZ progenitors (Figure 6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and illustrated in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The cardiac tube directly regulates core progenitors and in turn all MZ progenitors.
claims.source: While the PSC acts only on a subset of MZ progenitors (Baldeosingh et al., 2018; Oyallon et al., 2016), the cardiac tube directly regulates core progenitors and in turn all MZ progenitors (Figure 6).
claims.evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study illustrated in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The identification of two niches that differentially regulate lymph gland progenitors sheds further light on the parallels existing between Drosophila lymph gland and mammalian bone marrow hematopoiesis.
claims.source: The identification of two niches that differentially regulate lymph gland progenitors sheds further light on the parallels existing between Drosophila lymph gland and mammalian bone marrow hematopoiesis.
claims.evidence: This is a broader implication of the study's findings.

claims.claim: Btl-FGF signaling regulates trachea morphogenesis, which builds the insect respiratory system.
claims.source: Btl-FGF signaling regulates trachea morphogenesis, which builds the insect respiratory system (Glazer and Shilo, 1991; Klämbt et al., 1992; Muha and Müller, 2013; Sato and Kornberg, 2002; Sutherland et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on trachea development.

claims.claim: Studies on Drosophila larval Air-Sac-Primordium (ASP) brought to light a key role of long range direct cellular contacts mediated by long thin cellular extensions called cytonemes in Bnl delivery.
claims.source: Studies performed on Drosophila larval Air-Sac-Primordium (ASP), using endogenous tagged versions of Bnl and Btl, brought to light a key role of long range direct cellular contacts mediated by long thin cellular extensions called cytonemes (Roy et al., 2011; Sato and Kornberg, 2002).

claims.claim: Bnl produced by wing disc cells is delivered directly to ASP cells by cytonemes to activate FGF signaling.
claims.source: In this process, rather than diffusing passively, Bnl produced by wing disc cells is delivered directly to ASP cells by cytonemes to activate FGF signaling (Du et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: No cytoplasmic extensions from either cardiac cells or MZ progenitors were observed, ruling out the delivery of Bnl from cardiac cells though long cytoplasmic extensions.
claims.source: No cytoplasmic extensions from either cardiac cells or MZ progenitors were observed so far, ruling out the delivery of Bnl from cardiac cells though long cytoplasmic extensions.
claims.evidence: This is based on the absence of observed cytonemes in the lymph gland system.

claims.claim: Both cardiac cells and MZ progenitors are embedded in a dense network of extra-cellular matrix (ECM).
claims.source: Instead, both cardiac cells and MZ progenitors are embedded in a dense network of extra-cellular matrix (ECM) (Grigorian et al., 2013; Krzemień et al., 2007; Volk et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work on ECM in the lymph gland.

claims.claim: The Htl-FGF pathway is also required in MZ progenitors with a loss-of-function phenotype opposite to that of Btl-FGF inactivation.
claims.source: Interestingly, the Htl-FGF pathway is also required in MZ progenitors with a loss-of-function phenotype (Dragojlovic-Munther and Martinez-Agosto, 2013) opposite to that of to Btl-FGF inactivation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Htl-FGF signaling acts through Ras and MAPK activation.
claims.source: While Htl-FGF signaling acts through Ras and MAPK activation, we show here that Btl-FGF signaling controls intracellular calcium concentration in hematopoietic progenitors probably through PLCγ activation.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of Htl-FGF signaling.

claims.claim: There is absence of hierarchy between Htl-FGF and Btl-FGF signaling pathways in the MZ.
claims.source: By performing epistasis experiments, we further establish the absence of hierarchy between Htl-FGF and Btl-FGF signaling pathways in the MZ and that both pathways are required simultaneously to control lymph gland hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: Both Htl-FGF and Btl-FGF pathways are required simultaneously to control lymph gland hematopoiesis.

claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the epistasis experiment results.

claims.claim: This is the first example in which Btl and Htl are both expressed and required in the same cell population.

claims.claim: Simultaneous regulation by the two FGF pathways and a Bnl contribution by two separate tissues confers robustness to lymph gland hematopoiesis under normal developmental conditions and flexibility in response to environmental fluctuation.
claims.source: We postulate that simultaneous regulation by the two pathways and a Bnl contribution by two separate tissues confers robustness to lymph gland hematopoiesis under normal developmental conditions and flexibility in response to environmental fluctuation.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the biological significance of the findings.

claims.claim: FGF signaling controls both primitive and definitive hematopoiesis in vertebrates.
claims.source: In vertebrates, FGF signaling controls both primitive and definitive hematopoiesis (Dzierzak and Bigas, 2018; Muha and Müller, 2013; Ornitz and Itoh, 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on vertebrate FGF signaling.

claims.claim: FGFR1 in adult HSPCs is activated during hematopoietic recovery following injury, in order to stimulate HSPC proliferation and mobilization.
claims.source: Additional studies indicate that FGFR1 in adult HSPCs is activated during hematopoietic recovery following injury, in order to stimulate HSPC proliferation and mobilization (Zhao et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.source: Furthermore, FGF2 facilitates HSPC expansion by amplifying mesenchymal stem cells, a niche cell type (Itkin et al., 2013; Itkin et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: In vertebrate adult bone marrow, the FGF pathway plays a major role in the control of hematopoiesis both under steady state conditions and in response to an immune stress.
claims.source: Thus, in vertebrate adult bone marrow, the FGF pathway plays a major role in the control of hematopoiesis both under steady state conditions and in response to an immune stress.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the cited literature on FGF in bone marrow.

claims.claim: There is promise that the newly identified regulation of FGF signaling in the lymph gland will shed light on the complex regulation of FGF signaling in mammalian bone marrow.
claims.source: Given the high conservation of signaling pathways between Drosophila and mammals, the low genetic redundancy in Drosophila and the striking similarities between mammalian bone marrow and fly lymph gland, there is promise that our newly identified regulation of FGF signaling in the lymph gland will shed light on the complex regulation of FGF signaling in mammalian bone marrow.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about the broader implications of the findings.

results.result: The manuscript establishes the biological context for studying Drosophila hematopoiesis, describing the lymph gland structure, cell types, and known regulatory mechanisms including the PSC niche and heterogeneous progenitor populations.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C18 provide well-established background information supported by appropriate citations to prior literature and established knowledge. The anatomical descriptions are consistent with Figure 1a and prior work. These claims appropriately set up the rationale for investigating additional niche signals beyond the PSC.

results.result: An RNAi screen in cardiac cells identified 17 ligands affecting lymph gland homeostasis, classified into three phenotypic groups, with nine ligands validated using two independent cardiac drivers and shown to affect core progenitor maintenance.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C26 describe a systematic screen with appropriate controls (two independent drivers) and clear phenotypic classification. The data in Figure 1 support the quantified phenotypes for PSC cell numbers, crystal cell differentiation, and tep4 expression. Sample sizes appear adequate (at least 15 lymph glands per genotype) with statistical analysis performed.

results.result: The FGF ligand Branchless (bnl) is expressed in cardiac cells, pericardial cells, and weakly in MZ progenitors. Loss of bnl function in cardiac cells leads to increased blood cell differentiation and reduced progenitor marker expression, indicating that cardiac-derived Bnl controls lymph gland homeostasis in third instar larvae.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C34 are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including in situ hybridization (Figure 2a), genetic loss-of-function experiments with heterozygous mutants and RNAi (Figure 2b-r), temporal control experiments, and validation with multiple RNAi lines and drivers. The phenotypes are consistent and quantified with appropriate statistics.

results.result: Bnl is produced by both cardiac cells and MZ progenitors, with both sources contributing to lymph gland homeostasis. Cardiac-derived Bnl contributes to the MZ Bnl pool, and the level of cardiac Bnl controls hemocyte differentiation as shown by knockdown, overexpression, and rescue experiments.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C39 are supported by complementary experiments including progenitor-specific knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a-f), endogenous Bnl:GFP tracking showing reduced MZ signal when cardiac bnl is knocked down (Figure 2t-u), cardiac overexpression reducing crystal cells, and rescue experiments. The data converge to support dual sources of Bnl.

results.result: Cardiac cell-derived Bnl does not affect PSC cell numbers or Hedgehog activity, suggesting direct action on MZ progenitors rather than indirect effects through the PSC.
results.evaluation: Claim C40 is supported by data showing no changes in PSC markers (Antp, hhF4-GFP) when bnl is knocked down in cardiac cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2j-o). This is an important control establishing that the cardiac niche acts independently of the PSC niche.

results.result: The FGF receptor Breathless (btl) is expressed in cardiac cells and MZ progenitors. Btl function specifically in MZ progenitors (not cardiac cells) is required to control lymph gland homeostasis, as shown by loss-of-function, gain-of-function, and rescue experiments.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C49 are well-supported by expression analysis using btl:cherryendo knock-in (Figure 3a), heterozygous mutant analysis, tissue-specific RNAi showing progenitor-specific requirement, constitutively active receptor experiments, and rescue with btlCA. The lack of PSC effects provides appropriate controls. Multiple independent experiments converge on the same conclusion.

results.result: Epistasis experiments between Btl-FGF and Htl-FGF pathways show no hierarchy between them, suggesting both pathways act simultaneously in MZ progenitors to robustly regulate hemocyte differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C52 are supported by epistasis data (Figure 3n-p) showing that HtlDN and btl-RNAi together restore wildtype phenotype. However, C53 is speculative about robustness and flexibility without direct experimental evidence. The epistasis experiment is well-designed but the interpretation about simultaneous requirement and biological significance requires additional validation.

results.result: Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling mediates inter-organ communication between the vascular system and lymph gland progenitors, establishing the cardiac tube as a second niche that acts directly on MZ progenitors.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C55 represent the primary conclusion integrating results showing bnl expression in cardiac cells, btl expression in progenitors, and functional requirements in both tissues. The conclusion is well-supported by the combined genetic and expression data, though direct visualization of signaling would strengthen the claim.

results.result: Bnl::GFP secreted by cardiac cells is detected as cytoplasmic punctate dots in MZ progenitors that co-localize with Btl receptor and endosomal markers (Rab11, Rab7), suggesting receptor-mediated endocytosis. Blocking cardiac secretion with sar1-RNAi reduces Bnl::GFP in progenitors and increases blood cell differentiation, which is rescued by Bnl overexpression.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C64 are supported by co-localization data (Figure 4a-d), sar1 knockdown experiments affecting both Bnl distribution and phenotype (Figure 4e-k), and rescue experiments. The interpretation of receptor-mediated endocytosis is reasonable given the co-localization data, though direct functional tests of endocytosis would strengthen this conclusion. The sar1 experiments provide good evidence for secretion requirement.

results.result: Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling in progenitors does not involve MAPK or PI3K pathways but instead regulates intracellular Ca2+ levels. Btl knockdown in progenitors reduces Ca2+ levels in third instar larvae but not L2 stage, indicating the pathway is required for Ca2+ regulation in late larvae but not for progenitor specification.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C71 are supported by citation to prior work showing opposite phenotypes for MAPK/PI3K (C65), Ca2+ sensor measurements showing reduced GCaMP3 fluorescence with btl knockdown (Figure 5a-c), and temporal analysis at L2 vs L3 stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a-c). The logic connecting opposite phenotypes to exclude MAPK/PI3K is sound. The temporal data appropriately distinguish specification from maintenance functions.

results.result: Increasing intracellular Ca2+ in progenitors by overexpressing CaMKII or IP3R inhibits blood cell differentiation and rescues the btl knockdown phenotype, indicating that Ca2+ regulation functions downstream of Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C75 are supported by gain-of-function experiments with CaMKII and IP3R showing reduced crystal cells (Figure 5d-h, Figure 5—figure supplement 1d-h) and rescue experiments where Ca2+ elevation suppresses btl-RNAi phenotype. The epistasis logic is sound and the experiments are well-controlled. This establishes the pathway order: Bnl/Btl → Ca2+ → differentiation control.

results.result: PLCγ (encoded by small wing/sl) acts in MZ progenitors downstream of Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling to control Ca2+ levels and hemocyte differentiation, as shown by loss-of-function phenotypes and epistasis with constitutively active Btl.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C80 are supported by analysis of sl mutants and progenitor-specific RNAi showing increased differentiation (Figure 5i-m), and epistasis showing btlCA cannot rescue sl mutant phenotype (Figure 5k,n). This establishes the pathway: Bnl/Btl → PLCγ → Ca2+ → differentiation. The epistasis logic is appropriate and the experiments are well-designed.

results.result: The cardiac tube acts as a second niche alongside the PSC to control lymph gland homeostasis. While the PSC acts on a subset of progenitors, the cardiac tube directly regulates core progenitors and thereby all MZ progenitors through Bnl/Btl-FGF signaling that controls Ca2+ via PLCγ.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C89 represent the integrated conclusions of the study. They are well-supported by the combined data showing: (1) cardiac cells produce Bnl that acts on progenitors expressing Btl, (2) this pathway controls Ca2+ via PLCγ, (3) the pathway acts independently of the PSC, and (4) it specifically affects core progenitors. The model in Figure 6 appropriately summarizes these findings. The distinction between PSC and cardiac tube niches is well-established.

results.result: The identification of dual niches in Drosophila lymph gland parallels mammalian bone marrow with its endosteal and vascular niches. This is the first example of Btl and Htl co-expression in the same cells, and the findings may illuminate FGF regulation in mammalian hematopoiesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C90, C100, C101, and C107 are largely speculative about broader implications and novelty. While the parallel to mammalian dual niches is reasonable (C90), the claims about being the first example of Btl/Htl co-expression (C100) and future impact on understanding mammalian systems (C107) are not directly tested. C101 about robustness and flexibility is speculation without experimental evidence. These represent reasonable discussion points but are not experimentally validated.

results.result: Unlike Bnl delivery via cytonemes in trachea development, no cytoplasmic extensions were observed between cardiac cells and MZ progenitors. Instead, both cell types are embedded in dense ECM, suggesting an alternative mechanism for Bnl delivery.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C95 appropriately cite prior work on cytoneme-mediated Bnl delivery in other systems (C91-C93) and note the absence of such structures in the lymph gland (C94). The presence of ECM is supported by citations (C95). However, the negative observation (no cytonemes) should be interpreted cautiously as absence of evidence is not evidence of absence without systematic analysis.

results.result: Both Htl-FGF (acting through Ras/MAPK) and Btl-FGF (acting through PLCγ/Ca2+) pathways are required simultaneously in MZ progenitors with no hierarchy between them, representing a novel regulatory mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C99 integrate prior work on Htl-FGF (C96-C97) with current findings on Btl-FGF and epistasis experiments (C98-C99). The epistasis data support lack of hierarchy. However, the claim that both are required "simultaneously" (C99) is inferred from epistasis but not directly demonstrated by temporal or biochemical analysis of concurrent pathway activation.

results.result: FGF signaling plays major roles in vertebrate hematopoiesis under steady-state and stress conditions, but deciphering mechanisms is challenging due to multiple ligands, receptors, and redundancy in mammalian systems.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C106 appropriately summarize prior literature on FGF in vertebrate hematopoiesis with appropriate citations. These provide context for why the Drosophila system is valuable but do not represent findings of the current study.
